# requireService

<link-summary>Returns a service once it is known to exist, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireService() — Returns a service once it is known to exist, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript</code> · Since: 1.5.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireService<T>(
  service: T | null | undefined,
  message: string = "Service is not defined."
): T;
```

An advanced service that was never enabled is simply an undefined global, and the failure that follows is a `ReferenceError` far from its cause. This turns it into a named exception with a message that says what to switch on.

## Parameters

| Parameter                                            | Type                     | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `service`                                            | `T \| null \| undefined` | The service to check.                                         |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Service is not defined."` | `string`                 | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same service.

## Throws

| Exception                      | Condition                             |
| :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| `ServiceIsNotDefinedException` | the service is `null` or `undefined`. |

## Examples

### In use

```javascript
// An advanced service is a global that only exists once it has been enabled.
const directory = requireService(AdminDirectory, "Enable the Admin SDK service.");
```
